name: Cortexa
description: Cortexa is a precision-engineered neuromodulator that interfaces directly with BCI reward pathways, flooding the nucleus accumbens with a calibrated dopaminergic cascade while suppressing anxiety circuits. Unlike crude stimulants, it produces a clean, architectural euphoria — users describe it as 'feeling chosen.' Lazarus markets it as a 'cognitive wellness supplement' in Tier 4-5 lounges.
effects: Heightened sense of purpose and significance
BCI feedback loop amplification — music and visuals gain emotional weight
Sensation of mental clarity and superiority
side_effects: BCI feedback desynchronization with repeated use
Severe crash if dose is interrupted mid-cycle
cultural_context: Cortexa is the drug of the aspirational class — Tier 3 professionals who want to feel Tier 5 for an evening. Corporate social events in Tier 4 often have it available at the bar under a polite fiction. On the street, knockoff versions called 'Crown' circulate at half the price with unpredictable BCI compatibility, sometimes causing interface seizures.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 accountant has been sourcing black-market Cortexa for six months and begins experiencing 'the Throne effect' — a delusion of absolute correctness in every decision, leading to catastrophic professional choices
A Lazarus executive discovers that Cortexa's patent formula was stolen from a Shelf-based chemist who synthesized the compound first — and that chemist is now dead under suspicious circumstances
A runner is hired to steal a Cortexa production batch that has been reformulated without authorization — the new version doesn't just stimulate the reward pathway, it rewrites it
